$comment: THE HOUSEHOLD CONSTRAINT STORE (v6). This is the ACCOUNT's copy of household policy —
the source of truth. It pushes DOWN to the device on every dispatch; the device owns
world state (what is in the fridge, what has been spent) and never sources policy.
One entry per FACT, not per kind, so each carries its own provenance and lifetime:
kind         which constraints.hard / soft key it resolves into
value        list | number | string | window object
enforcement  hard = the Safety filter blocks on it · soft = planning bias only
source       account (a person entered it) | derived (real-world data) | chat (captured)
scope        household | domain | goal
applies_to   domains this entry is picked for; ['*'] = every domain
expires_day_offset  retires itself this many days from today (omit = permanent)
RESOLUTION (memory/store.py — deterministic, no LLM):
- hard LIST kinds (allergens, dietary, medical) are UNIONED across every entry,
applies_to IGNORED. The enforced set is never narrowed by relevance: a wrong
relevance pick must cost a noisy plan, never a safety miss.
- hard SCALAR kinds (budget_cap, quiet_hours, peak_hours, away_window) ARE
domain-picked: most specific applies_to wins, ties go to the stricter value.
- soft entries are picked by relevance (LLM, with applies_to as the fallback).
Dates are DAY OFFSETS resolved against today at load — the same generic-clock rule the
device data files follow. Absolute dates go stale between demos.

$comment: THE HOUSEHOLD ENVELOPE (v6-M3). Per-goal caps alone cannot stop two goals
spending the same money: a $200 party and a $120 grocery week each fit their own
ceiling and together blow a month. This is the shared pool they both draw from.
The device resolves the goal's EFFECTIVE cap as min(domain cap, envelope - spent)
at arm time and again on approval and each day tick — the cap is policy from here,
the spend is world state the device owns.
constraints.label: monthly household envelope
constraints.note: derived from the account's spending history

$comment: Peak tariff. Scoped to energy_saving ON PURPOSE: a peak-hour dishwasher run defeats
THAT goal's own objective, whereas blocking it household-wide would kill the guest-
dinner cleanup beat (21:00 sits inside the peak window) for no safety reason.
Enforced by the EXISTING time_window_block rule kind — no new device code (M2).

constraints.note: time-of-use tariff on the utility account

$comment: The away window, derived from the trip in the shared calendar. Offsets match the
device's data/vacation.json (depart +1, return +8).
SCOPED TO vacation_prep, not ['*'], and that is a deliberate limit: the seeded world
has the family eating dinners at home on days 1-6 AND away on days 1-8, so a
household-wide away window would block the meal demo's appliance proposals. Widening
it to ['*'] — which is the more honest rule, and would catch a meal goal preheating
the oven mid-trip — requires the world data to agree on when the family is away first.
constraints.label: away window
